choices.title: Tetralogy of Fallot
choices.correct_explanation:
• Tetralogy of fallot is a cyanotic heart disease because there is reduction in arterial oxygen saturation and the baby becomes cyanosed. The four problems of tetralogy of Fallot are:
    • Ventricular septal defect (VSD): A ventricular septal defect (VSD), a hole in the heart, is a heart defect that's present at birth (congenital). The hole (defect) occurs in the wall septum that separates the heart's lower chambers (ventricles) and allows blood to pass from the left to the right side of the heart. The oxygen-rich blood then gets pumped back to the lungs instead of out of the body, causing the heart to work harder.
    • Pulmonary Stenosis: A narrowing or thickening of the valve that connects the right ventricle to the pulmonary artery, the blood vessel that carries low-oxygen blood from the heart to the lungs. Due to pulmonary stenosis heart has to work harder.
    • Right ventricular hypertrophy: Right ventricular hypertrophy is a thickening of the muscular wall of the right ventricle. The thickened wall can contribute to blocking the flow of blood through the pulmonary valve, which allows blood from the heart to flow into the lungs.
    • Overriding aorta: An overriding aorta is a congenital heart defect where the aorta is positioned directly over a ventricular septal defect, instead of over the left ventricle.
  • The ductus arteriosus is a normal fetal artery connecting the main body artery (aorta) and the main lung artery (pulmonary artery). The ductus allows blood to detour away from the lungs before birth. After birth, the opening is no longer needed and it usually narrows and closes within the first few days. When the ductus arteriosus stays open, oxygen-rich (red) blood passes from the aorta to the pulmonary artery, mixing with the oxygen-poor (blue) blood already flowing to the lungs. The blood vessels in the lungs have to handle a larger amount of blood than normal. It increases lung pressure and cause breathing difficulty in children.
  • An atrial septal defect (ASD) is a hole in the wall between the two upper chambers of heart (atria). The condition is present at birth (congenital). An atrial septal defect (ASD) allows freshly oxygenated blood to flow from the left upper chamber of the heart (left atrium) into the right upper chamber of the heart (right atrium). There, it mixes with deoxygenated blood and is pumped to the lungs, even though it's already refreshed with oxygen.

This causes pumping chambers in heart (the ventricles) to quiver uselessly, instead of pumping blood. No heartbeat or weak heartbeat is main sign of ventricular tachycardia, which is the main cause of sudden death in patients with myocardial infarction.
    • CPR is an emergency procedure that combines chest compressions often with artificial ventilation. It maintains blood flow to the organs until an electrical shock (defibrillation) can be given.
    • The most common treatment is defibrillation, which uses special paddles to apply a charge to the heart from an external electrical source in an attempt to establish a normal sinus rhythm.

Figure: Ventricular fibrillation

  • Premature ventricular contraction: Premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) are extra heartbeats that begin in two lower pumping chambers (ventricles). These extra beats disrupt regular heart rhythm, sometimes causing to feel a fluttering or a skipped beat in chest.
  • Atrial fibrillation: Atrial fibrillation meaning that the problem occurs above the ventricles. For atrial fibrillation, the abnormal heart rhythms are due to irregular electrical activity in the atria, mainly the right atrium. It usually results in a fast and irregular heartbeat.
  • Atrioventricular block: Atrioventricular block (AV block) is a type of heart block in which the conduction between the atria and ventricles of the heart is impaired.
    In premature ventricular contraction, atrial fibrillation, atrioventricular block may automatically revert to normal sinus rhythm or can be rectified with medication.

    • Type 2 diabetes (formerly named non-insulin-dependent) which results from the body's inability to respond properly to the action of insulin produced by the pancreas. Type 2 diabetes is much more common and accounts for around 90% of all diabetes cases worldwide. It occurs most frequently in adults but is being noted increasingly in adolescents as well.
    • Diabetes insipidus is a rare disorder that occurs when kidney passes an abnormally large volume of urine that is insipid—dilute and odorless. When damage to hypothalamus or pituitary gland causes disruptions in the normal production, storage, and release of vasopressin.     • Example: O2 and CO2, electrolytes, vitamins and water are transported across placenta by diffusion.
    • Oxygen is a small molecule which readily crosses the placenta by passive diffusion. Oxygen transfer mainly depends on the partial pressure gradient of oxygen between maternal blood in the intervillous space and fetal blood in the umbilical arteries.

  • Note: Passive transport is a movement of ions and other atomic or molecular substances across cell membranes without need of energy input.
  • Facilitated transport is the process of spontaneous passive transport of molecules or ions across a biological membrane via specific transmembrane integral proteins.
    • Example: Glucose, fatty acids and vitamins are transported by facilitated transport across the placenta.
  • Active transport is the movement of ions and molecules across a cell membrane into a region of higher concentration, assisted by enzymes and requiring energy.
    • Example: Electrolytes, calcium, vitamins, and amino acids are transported by active transport across the placenta.
  • Pinocytosis is the method by which a cell absorbs small particles outside the cell and brings them inside.

  • Infections caused by protozoa are commonly parasitic diseases caused by organisms such as Entamoeba histolytica, Plasmodium.
  • Common fungal infections are caused by yeasts such as candida or Malassezia furfur.
  • Common bacterial infections are meningitis, otitis media, pneumonia and tuberculosis.

questions.title: Warts are caused by _____.

choices.title: Pulmonary embolism
choices.correct_explanation:
• Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) occurs when a blood clot (thrombus) forms in one or more of the deep veins in body, usually in legs. It can cause leg pain or swelling. Thrombus from legs can travel to the lungs, which obstruct the pulmonary artery and produce pulmonary embolism (PE).
  • Shock is caused by decreased blood, oxygen and nutrient supply to the cell and organs.
  • Heart attack happens when there is a sudden complete blockage of an artery due to atherosclerosis.
  • A stroke occurs when the blood supply to the part of brain is interrupted or reduced, which causes brain cell death.

questions.title: Deep vein thrombosis renders a person at a risk of:

choices.title: Mitochondria
choices.correct_explanation:
• Mitochondria are referred as powerhouse of cell. Synthesis of ATP takes place in mitochondria. This ATP is used as the source of energy by the cell; therefore Mitochondria are referred as “power house of cell”.
  • Lysosomes are membrane-enclosed vesicles that form the Golgi complex. It contains hydrolytic enzymes, involved in digestion and waste removal.
  • Nucleus the primary functions of the nucleus are to store the cell’s DNA, maintain its integrity, and facilitate its transcription and replication.
  • Golgi apparatus is a complex of vesicles and folded membranes within the cytoplasm of cells. It is involved in secretion and intracellular transport.

questions.title: Which of the following is referred as the powerhouse of the cell?

choices.title: Vital, Essential, Desirable
choices.correct_explanation:
• Vital, Essential, Desirable: VED analysis is a technique in inventory control. It divides inventory into three groups: vital items, essential items and desirable items
    • V—Vital items: Without which an institution cannot function. It is stocked in abundance
    • E—Essential items: Without which an institute can function but may affect the quality of service. Essential items are stocked in medium amount.
    • D—Desirable items: It is stocked in small amounts
  • Remaining options are mere distractors.

questions.title: VED stands for:

choices.title: Mode
choices.correct_explanation:
• Mode is the number which appears most often (Highest frequency) in a set of numbers.
    Example: in {6, 3, 9, 6, 6, 5, 9, 3} the Mode is 6 (it occurs most often).
  • Mean is the average of the numbers a calculated "central" value of a set of numbers.
    First add up all the numbers and then divide by how many numbers there are.
    Example: 2, 7, 9
       2 + 7 + 9 = 18/3 = 6
  • Standard deviation is a measure that is used to quantify the amount of variation or dispersion of a set of data values.
  • The median is a simple measure of central tendency. (middle number)

questions.title: The value of highest frequency in the data is:

choices.title: Restraint
choices.correct_explanation:
• Restraint is a device that restricts movement, keep person in proper position and prevents harmful behavior.
  • Crutches are a type of walking aids that serve to increase the individual’s base of support. It is used to aid in mobilization. There are mainly two types of crutches—axillary crutchesand elbow crutches. Gutter crutches are the third additional type of crutches.
  • Canes are walking stick used as a crutch or mobility aid. Canes can help redistribute weight from a lower leg that is weak or painful, improve stability by increasing the base of support, and provide tactile information about the ground to improve balance.
  • Pillow is a comfort device used to keep body at alignment, use under head, arms, legs and along spine.

questions.title: Device used to aid immobilization of a patient is called:

choices.title: Keratitis
choices.correct_explanation:
• Keratitis is an inflammation of the cornea. The cornea is the clear front surface of the eye. It lies directly in front of the iris and pupil, and it allows light to enter the eye. Causes of keratitis are infection, dry eyes, physical and chemical injury and foreign body in eye.
  • Conjunctivitis is an inflammation of conjunctiva caused by bacteria (Staphylococcus aureus) and virus [herpes simplex virus (HSV)].
  • Trachoma is a disease of the eye caused by infection with the bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis. It can cause blindness.
  • Scleritis is a serious inflammatory disease that affects the white outer coating of the eye, known as the sclera. It is an autoimmune disorder or can cause by eye infection, connective tissue disease.

questions.title: Inflammation of cornea is called:

choices.title: Acetyl CoA
choices.correct_explanation:
• Ketogenesis is the biochemical process through which organisms produce ketone bodies through breakdown of fatty acids and ketogenic amino acids. The production of ketone bodies is initiated to make available energy that is stored as fatty acids. Fatty acids are enzymatically broken down in β-oxidationto form acetyl-CoA. Under normal conditions, acetyl-CoA is further oxidized by the citric acid cycle (TCA/Krebs cycle) and then by the mitochondrial electron transport chain to release energy.
  • Cholesterol is a waxy, fat-like substance that is found in the bod
  • Phospholipids are a class of lipids that are a major component of all cell membranes.
  • A triglyceride is the major form of fat stored in the body. It consists of three molecules of fatty acid combined with a molecule of the alcohol glycerol.

questions.title: Ketone bodies are synthesized from:

choices.title: Calcium
choices.correct_explanation:
• The chief element involved in clotting of blood is Calcium (Ca++), which is the 4th clotting factor. It helps in conversion of prothrombin to thrombin, which is essential for clot formation.
  • Magnesium helps to maintain normal nerve and muscle function, supports a healthy immune system, keeps the heart beat steady, and helps in bones strengthening. It also helps to regulate blood glucose levels and aid in the production of energy and protein.
  • Potassium is one of the most important minerals in the body. It helps regulate fluid balance, muscle contractions and nerve signals.
  • Sodium is important for muscle and nerve function and helps to maintain stable blood pressure level.

questions.title: Mineral required for clotting of blood is:

choices.title: Nosocomial infection
choices.correct_explanation:
• Nosocomial infection is an infection that is acquired in hospital. This infection is strictly and specifically an infection "not present prior to hospital admission, but generally occurs 48 hours after admission."
  • Communicable disease is spread from one person to another through different ways that include — contact with blood and bodily fluids, breathing in an airborne infection.
  • Wound infections refer to infection from wound. The infection is caused by the purulent discharge that drains from the wound.
  • Droplet infection is an infection transmitted from one individual to another by droplets of moisture expelled from the upper respiratory tract through sneezing or coughing by the infected person.

questions.title: Hospital-acquired infection is called:

choices.title: Hernia
choices.correct_explanation:
• Hernia is a condition in which part of an organ is displaced and protrudes through the wall of the cavity. (Often involving the intestine at a weak point in the abdominal wall).
  • Adhesion is the union of two opposing tissue surfaces.
  • Volvulus refers to abnormal twisting of a part of the large or small intestine and this twisting may lead to bowel obstruction.
  • Intussusception is a condition in which one segment of intestine slips into another portion located below it, just like telescope, which causes intestinal obstruction.

questions.title: Abnormal protrusion or projection of an organ through a weakness in abdomen is referred as:

choices.title: Brain auditory pathways
choices.correct_explanation:
• Central hearing loss results from damage of brain auditory pathways.
  • Brain auditory pathways consist of different structures; these are cochlear nucleus, superior olivary complex, lateral lemniscus, inferior colliculus, thalamus and auditory cortex in temporal lobe. Central hearing loss is caused by a lesion in the central auditory pathway or in the auditory cortex. The auditory cortex processes and interprets the sounds amplified and received by the ossicles and cochlear hair cells.
  • Olfactory nerve is the 1st cranial nerve, which conveys special sensory information related to smell. If olfactory nerve damaged, anosmia (loss of smell) occurs.
  • The facial nerve is the 7th cranial nerve for facial expression. If facial nerve damaged, it leads to Bell's palsy (one-sided face paralysis).
  • The auditory nerve [Vestibulocochlear (8th cranial nerve)] has two branches—vestibular branch and cochlear branch. Vestibular branch carries impulses for equilibrium and cochlear branch carries impulses for hearing.

questions.title: Central hearing loss results from damage of:

choices.title: Cellulitis
choices.correct_explanation:
• Cellulitis is a bacterial infection of underlying layers of the skin and the site of infection turns red with swelling and pain.
  • Abscess is a localized collection of pus in tissues, organs, or confined spaces usually because of infection.
  • Boil is skin abscess that forms at a hair follicle infected with pus-forming bacteria.
  • Ulcers are open sore on external or internal surface of the body caused by break in the skin or mucous membrane.
